67482-a-handbook-of-cookery-for-a-small-.title: A Handbook Of Cookery For A Small House
67482-a-handbook-of-cookery-for-a-small-.creator: Unknown
67482-a-handbook-of-cookery-for-a-small-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The bane of life in a small house is the smell of cooking. Very few are free from it. And yet it need not be endured at all. This evil yields to nothing more heroic than a simple but scrupulous care in all the processes in making food ready for consumption. That is why your constant presence in the kitchen is recommended.

7242-a-connecticut-yankee-in-king-arthur.title: A Connecticut Yankee In King Arthur'S Court
7242-a-connecticut-yankee-in-king-arthur.creator: Unknown
7242-a-connecticut-yankee-in-king-arthur.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. It was in Warwick Castle that I came across the curious stranger whom I am going to talk about. He attracted me by three things: his candid simplicity, his marvelous familiarity with ancient armor, and the restfulness of his company--for he did all the talking.

arxiv-2303-11079.title: Differentially Private Algorithms for Synthetic Power System Datasets
arxiv-2303-11079.creator: Vladimir Dvorkin, Audun Botterud
arxiv-2303-11079.description: Abstract While power systems research relies on the availability of real-world network datasets, data owners (e.g., system operators) are hesitant to share data due to security and privacy risks. To control these risks, we develop privacy-preserving algorithms for the synthetic generation of optimization and machine learning datasets.

arxiv-2305-05403.title: Completeness, Recall, and Negation in Open-World Knowledge Bases: A Survey Volume: 0 0 0 CCS: General and reference Surveys and overviews CCS: Computing methodologies Knowledge representation and reasoning CCS: Computing methodologies Artificial intelligence
arxiv-2305-05403.creator: Simon Razniewski, Hiba Arnaout, Shrestha Ghosh, Fabian Suchanek
arxiv-2305-05403.description: Abstract . General-purpose knowledge bases (KBs) are a cornerstone of knowledge-centric AI. Many of them are constructed pragmatically from web sources, and are thus far from complete. This poses challenges for the consumption as well as the curation of their content.

arxiv-2406-18337.title: The Geometry of Generalised Spin r Spinors on Projective Spaces
arxiv-2406-18337.creator: Diego ARTACHO a and Jordan HOFMANN b
arxiv-2406-18337.description: Abstract In this paper, we adapt the characterisation of the spin representation via exterior forms to the generalised spin r context. We find new invariant spin r spinors on the projective spaces ℂ ​ ℙ n \mathbb{CP}^{n} , ℍ ​ ℙ n \mathbb{HP}^{n} , and the Cayley plane 𝕆 ​ ℙ 2 \mathbb{OP}^{2} for all their homogeneous realisations.

arxiv-2412-21176.title: Classical J ​ T ¯ J\bar{T} symmetries – three ways – and a precision holography check
arxiv-2412-21176.creator: Silvia Georgescu, Monica Guica § Department of Mathematics, King’s College London, Strand, London, WC2R 2LS, United Kingdom, Université Paris-Saclay, CNRS, CEA, Institut de Physique Théorique, 91191 Gif-sur-Yvette, France, Institute of Physics, Ecole Polytechnique Fedérale de Lausanne, CH-1015 Lausa
arxiv-2412-21176.description: Abstract The J ​ T ¯ J\bar{T} deformation is a fully tractable irrelevant deformation of two-dimensional CFTs, which yields a UV-complete QFT that is local and conformal along one lightlike direction and non-local along the remaining one. Such QFTs are interesting, in particular, as toy models for the holographic dual to (near)-extremal black holes.

arxiv-2503-03683.title: First Limits on Light Dark Matter Interactions in a Low Threshold Two Channel Athermal Phonon Detector from the TESSERACT Collaboration
arxiv-2503-03683.creator: T.K. Bui, C.L. Chang, Y.-Y. Chang, L. Chaplinsky, C.W. Fink, M. Garcia-Sciveres, W. Guo, S.A. Hertel, X. Li, J. Lin, M. Lisovenko, R. Mahapatra, W. Matava, D.N. McKinsey, V. Novati, P.K. Patel, B. Penning, H.D. Pinckney, M. Platt, M. Pyle, Y. Qi, M. Reed, G.R.C Rischbieter, R.K. Romani, B. Sadoulet,
arxiv-2503-03683.description: Abstract We present results of a search for spin-independent dark matter-nucleon interactions in a 1 cm 2 by 1 mm thick (0.233 gram) high-resolution silicon athermal phonon detector operated above ground. For interactions in the substrate, this detector achieves a r.m.s. baseline energy resolution of 361.5 ± 4 meV 361.

arxiv-2505-13998.title: Empirical Validation of Functional Multidimensional Scaling via Numerical Simulation and Real-World Application
arxiv-2505-13998.creator: Liting Li
arxiv-2505-13998.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Liting Li. This article presents an empirical validation of the functional multidimensional scaling model, a novel approach that improves the smoothness of time-varying dissimilarities in a low-dimensional space, embedding a modified Adam stochastic gradient descent method. We conduct a numerical simulation study to evaluate the feasibility of the functional multidimensional scaling model under various controlled scenarios and to assess the goodness of the approximation of the estimators with a curvilinear search method, demonstrating its robustness and scalability in dynamic structures.

arxiv-2512-19703.title: ASK: Adaptive Self-improving Knowledge Framework for Audio Text Retrieval
arxiv-2512-19703.creator: Siyuan Fu, Xuchen Guo, Mingjun LiuHongxiang LiBoyin TanGongxi ZhuXianwei ZhuangJinghan Ru, Yuxin XieYuguo Yin
arxiv-2512-19703.description: Abstract The dominant paradigm for Audio-Text Retrieval (ATR) relies on mini-batch-based contrastive learning. This process, however, is inherently limited by what we formalize as the Gradient Locality Bottleneck (GLB), which structurally prevents models from leveraging out-of-batch knowledge and thus impairs fine-grained and long-tail learning.

arxiv-2601-16082.title: Roche limit and stellar disruption in the Simpson–Visser spacetime
arxiv-2601-16082.creator: Marcos V. de S. Silva
arxiv-2601-16082.description: Abstract Due to the tidal forces that a black hole can produce, certain types of compact objects may undergo disruption as they approach the black hole. This disruption point is known as the Roche limit (or Roche radius). In this work, we studied the tidal forces arising from the presence of the Simpson–Visser black bounce.

arxiv-2601-21336.title: Cross-correlating galaxies and cosmic dispersion measures: Constraints on the gas-to-halo mass relation from 2MASS galaxies and 133 localized fast radio bursts
arxiv-2601-21336.creator: Masato Shirasaki \altemailmark, Ryuichi Takahashi, Ken Osato, and Kunihito Ioka
arxiv-2601-21336.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Masato Shirasaki \altemailmark, Ryuichi Takahashi, Ken Osato, and Kunihito Ioka. We conduct a cross-correlation analysis between large-scale structures traced by the Two Micron All Sky Survey (2MASS) galaxy catalog and the cosmic dispersion measures of 133 localized fast radio bursts (FRBs). The cross-correlation signal is measured as a function of the comoving separation R R between 2MASS galaxies and background FRB sightlines, making full use of the available redshift information for both datasets.

britannica-1911-pagan-burma.description: Article 'Pagan (Burma)' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 20), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. It was founded by King Pyinbya in 847, and remained the capital until the extinction of the dynasty in 1298. Pagan itself is now a mere village, but hundreds of pagodas in various stages of decay meet the eye in every direction. The majority of them were built by King Anawra-hta, who overcame the Peguan king, Manuha of Thaton.

pmc-11388143.title: Biofilm Disruption from within: Light-Activated Molecular Drill-Functionalized Polymersomes Bridge the Gap between Membrane Damage and Quorum Sensing-Mediated Cell Death
pmc-11388143.creator: Bela B. Berking, Sjoerd J. Rijpkema, Bai H. E. Zhang, Arbaaz Sait, Helene Amatdjais-Groenen, Daniela A. Wilson
pmc-11388143.description: Bacterial biofilms represent an escalating global health concern with the proliferation of drug resistance and hospital-acquired infections annually. Numerous strategies are under exploration to combat biofilms and preempt the development of antibacterial resistance. Among these, mechanical disruption of biofilms and enclosed bacteria presents a promising avenue, aiming to induce membrane permeabilization and consequent lethal damage.

pmc-11545869.creator: Clarissa Pedrini Schuch, Lazar I Jovanovic, Gustavo Balbinot, Alan H Daniels
pmc-11545869.description: Disruptions in the brain’s connections to the hands resulting from a cervical spinal cord injury (cSCI) can lead to severe and persistent functional impairments. The integrity of these connections is an important predictor of upper extremity recovery in stroke and may similarly act as a biomarker in cSCI.

pmc-12579829.title: Reduced Attentional Capture by Topological Changes in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: Evidence for a Perceptual Deficit
pmc-12579829.creator: Jing Li, Huanjun Xi, Qingqing Zhang, Tao Duan, Dandan Li, Lei Shi, Shuoqiu Gan, Hong Li, Chunyan Zhu
pmc-12579829.description: BackgroundDeficits in the adaptive allocation of attention are considered a feature associated with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). It remains unclear whether the attention of children with ASD can be modulated involuntarily by stimulus-driven processes. Visual processing is believed to initiate with topological perception; thus, we investigate the modulation of attention shifts in children with ASD by altering topological properties.

pmc-12595315.title: Activation of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) by pioglitazone in oral traumatic ulcers in female rats
pmc-12595315.creator: Roque Soares Martins Neto, Lívia Victor da Silva, Clarice Lioba de Araújo, Angelo Gabriel Farias Valente, Antonio Alexandre Coelho, Caio Ferreira Freire Caetano, Gabriella Alves Julião Costa, Paulo Goberlânio de Barros Silva, Rafael Linard Avelar
pmc-12595315.description: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of pioglitazone treatment on oral ulcer healing in rats, given its potential to modulate inflammatory processes. Thirty-two animals were randomly allocated into four groups: one control and three treated with different doses of pioglitazone (5, 15, and 45 mg/kg).

pmc-13003750.title: Association between serum uric acid and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD): an observational cross-sectional study in an Egyptian outpatient cohort
pmc-13003750.creator: Haitham A. Mahmoud, W. Mohamed Abd Elghany, Mohammed Abdelhakeem, Hasnaa M. Ahmed, Nady Semeda, Safaa M Abdelhalim, Alaa M Mostafa, Shaimaa H Zaki, Manar M Sayed, Omar Abdelazim
pmc-13003750.description: BackgroundHepatic steatosis, characterized by excessive triglyceride accumulation within hepatocytes, is the central feature of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). This spectrum encompasses simple steatosis, non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), progressive fibrosis, and cirrhosis. NAFLD pathogenesis involves an intricate interplay between nutritional factors, metabolic dysregulation, and genetic predisposition.

pmc-13265600.title: The effect of canagliflozin on hippocampal dendrite morphology in a model of Alzheimer’s disease induced by intracerebroventricular injection of streptozotocin
pmc-13265600.creator: Sevdenur Yazi, Berna Ozen, Bahar Buldu, Ebru Yalcin, Osman Karakose, Ozan Cakmak, Selenay Somunkiran, Hasan R Yananli, Umit S Sehirli, Ozlem Kirazli
pmc-13265600.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and diabetes mellitus (DM) share common pathophysiological features. However, the effects of antidiabetic drugs on neurodegeneration are not completely known. Canagliflozin, a novel option for DM treatment, is a dual inhibitor of sodium glucose co-transporter type 2 (SGLT2) and acetylcholinesterase.

pmc-13300398.creator: F Buoncristiani, M Nesti, L Panchetti, S Garibaldi, G Mirizzi, A Agresti, C Angheben, G Grifoni, F Ferraris, A Giomi, A Santoro, F Landra, G Ricciardi, P Marchese, A Rossi
pmc-13300398.description: BackgroundThe optimal ablation strategy for patients undergoing repeat catheter ablation (CA) for atrial fibrillation (AF) remains debated. Vein of Marshall ethanol infusion (VOM-EI) has been proposed to enhance substrate modification and improve long-term rhythm control, particularly in patients with persistent AF (PeAF), but its role in repeated ablations is poorly investigated.
